title: Fixed-base-ideal extension categories and normalized kernel-pushout functors
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $X,B,B'$ algebraic spaces over it with their small etale sites [def-trf-algebraic-space], and use their module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Use square-zero algebra extensions and normalized site models [def-sfb-space-square-zero-extension-data], and normalized ideal presentations [def-sfb-space-square-zero-stalk-data]. A coefficient-changing extension map from $E$ with kernel $F$ to $D$ with kernel $G$, over $u:F\to G$, is a natural unital ring map $a:E\to D$ preserving the base algebra map and quotient to $\mathcal O_X$ and satisfying $a i_F=i_Gu$. For a fixed kernel these form a category, using identity and composition of the ring maps. Fix $i:B\to B'$, a normalized site model $T$ and a square-zero ideal presentation $J$ of its quotient, and $f:X\to B$. Use the canonical tensor pullback and its normalized local tensors [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. A fixed base-ideal map is represented by an $\mathcal O_X$-linear map $c:f^*J\to F$; by scalar-extension adjunction this is the same as an $f^{-1}\mathcal O_B$-linear map $f^{-1}J\to F$. The category of fixed-ideal extensions is the full subcategory of square-zero extensions for $X\to B'$ whose base action on $j\in J(V)$, on every compatible chart $q:U\to V$, is $i_F(c(1\otimes j))$. The map to the lifted chart $T^{-1}V$ is the composite of $q$ with the normalized reduction arrow; the equality is required on every such chart square. For $u:F\to G$, a functor $P$ from the fixed-$c$ category to the fixed-$uc$ category is kernel pushout if it has natural extension maps $a_E:E\to P(E)$ over $u$ such that for every module $H$, every extension $L$ over $X\to B'$ with kernel $H$, every $v:G\to H$ and extension map $b:E\to L$ over $vu$, there is a unique extension map $d:P(E)\to L$ over $v$ with $d a_E=b$. This is a definition with no existence assertion or choice of extension objects.
